Standard: The air vehicle has ground handling characteristics that are no worse than qualitative Level 2 when taxiing aboard ships. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis to verify the pilot and air vehicle are able to taxi in confined spaces on land and aboard ships with various obstacles (e.g., other air vehicles and arresting wire), and in precise control scenarios (e.g., catapult lineup and parking), including direction control power, braking performance, aerodynamic effects, engine power and control, and timing delays from command (e.g., from the air vehicle director) to vehicle response for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: surface conditions (e.g., tire friction, wet, oil), ship motion, and WOD from all relative directions. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Mission representative ground handling tasks include maneuvering in the tight confines of the carrier hangar and flight deck, during flight deck taxiing, during shipboard long taxi, while performing final alignment on the catapult and in tight turns (e.g., catapult spin-out and deck edge parking), during low speed taxi on a pitching deck, when clearing the landing area following shipboard arrested landings, and as specified in SA FTM-01, Flight and Hangar Deck Handling and Wing Fold/Sweep and Canopy Operations paragraphs. Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation of mission representative ground handling tasks to verify the pilot and air vehicle are able to taxi in confined spaces aboard ships with various obstacles (e.g., other air vehicles and arresting wire), and in precise control scenarios (e.g., catapult lineup and parking) for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: surface conditions (e.g., tire friction, wet, oil), ship motion, and WOD from all relative directions. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct shore-based piloted evaluations of mission representative ground handling tasks to verify the pilot and air vehicle are able to taxi in confined spaces aboard ships with various obstacles (e.g., other air vehicles and arresting wire), and in precise control scenarios (e.g., catapult lineup and parking) for all control modes across selected combinations of air vehicle states, control modes, environmental conditions: surface conditions (e.g., tire friction, wet, oil) and winds from all relative directions.
  (3) Flight test: Conduct shipboard piloted evaluations of mission representative ground handling tasks to verify the pilot and air vehicle are able to taxi in confined spaces aboard ships with various obstacles (e.g., other air vehicles and arresting wire), and in precise control scenarios (e.g., catapult lineup and parking) for all control modes across selected combinations of air vehicle states, environmental conditions, and ship conditions: surface conditions (e.g., tire friction, wet, oil), ship motion, and WOD from all relative directions.
